subject: The place from above — a high vantage before anything happens
reason: The {item} gets the whole place in one frame. Find height first: stairs, a bridge, a rooftop.

subject: Steam off the cup, backlit
reason: Steam only shows against the light. Put the window or the sun behind the cup.

subject: Hands doing one small task — sliding a door, tying a lace, turning a key
reason: Hands carry a sequence without showing a face. Cheap to get, always useful in the edit.

subject: Walking away from camera, through frame
reason: Movement without a face. Lock off and let them walk out of frame — it gives you a clean cut point.

subject: Empty street, leading lines
reason: Early enough and the street is yours. Put the vanishing point on a third.

subject: A texture — stone, weave, grain, rust
reason: The {item} turns a wall into a frame. Side light brings texture out; flat light hides it.

fallback.subject: A texture, as close as the lens will focus
fallback.reason: No macro packed — get as close as it focuses and crop in the edit.

subject: Timelapse — clouds over the skyline
reason: Locked off on the {item}: a 2-second interval for 10 minutes gives you 10 seconds of time passing.

fallback.subject: Timelapse from a wall or a railing
fallback.reason: No tripod — wedge the camera on something solid and don't touch it for ten minutes.

subject: Through a doorway — in on one, out on another
reason: Two doorways shot the same way cut together as one move. Match the framing, not the door.

subject: The scene upside down in a puddle or a window
reason: Get the lens low, almost touching the water. After rain this is free.

subject: A silhouette against the last of the light
reason: Expose for the sky and let them go black. Works at any presence level — nobody is recognisable.

subject: Point of view, walking in
reason: Arrival from your own eyes. Walk slowly and bend your knees — it hides most of the bounce.

subject: Push past something in the foreground to reveal the scene
reason: The {item} makes the push smooth enough to open on. Start close on a plant, a post, a shoulder.

fallback.subject: Pan off something in the foreground to reveal the scene
fallback.reason: No gimbal — a slow pan off a foreground object does the same job.

subject: Rack focus — foreground to background
reason: The {item} opens wide enough for the background to melt. Pull focus slowly — about two seconds.

subject: Signs and their reflections after dark
reason: The {item} holds the shot past dusk without the grain taking over.

subject: Drone pull-back — from the subject out to the whole place
reason: The {item} ends the piece by showing how small it all was. Check the wind and local rules first.

subject: Piece to camera — say where you are and why
reason: The {item} keeps your voice clean over the street. Get two takes, one shorter than you think.

subject: Walk and talk
reason: The {item} stays close to the mouth while you move. Walk slower than feels natural.

subject: A reaction — tasting, seeing, laughing
reason: Reactions are what people remember. Keep rolling after the moment — the real one comes late.

subject: A cutaway of exactly what you're talking about
reason: Every sentence you say to camera needs a picture to cut to. Shoot it straight after, while you remember.

subject: Hero shot of the product on a clean surface
reason: Locked off on the {item} so the product stays sharp and still. Clean the surface — it shows.

fallback.subject: Hero shot of the product, braced on the table edge
fallback.reason: No tripod — rest the camera on the table edge and hold for ten seconds.

subject: The product in someone's hands, being used
reason: Brands want their thing in a life, not on a table. Hands are enough.

subject: Logo or label, close
reason: The {item} gets the label sharp edge to edge. Clients check for this one.

fallback.subject: Logo or label, as close as the lens focuses
fallback.reason: No macro — get as close as it focuses; you'll crop in.

subject: The pour, in slow motion
reason: Your {item} shoots fast enough to slow the pour right down. Light it from behind.

fallback.subject: The pour, real speed, three takes
fallback.reason: No high frame rate — do three pours at real speed and pick the cleanest.

subject: Say the brand's name to camera
reason: Usually contracted, and easy to forget on the day. Say it three ways, with the {item} close.

subject: Interview — main angle, eyeline just off camera
reason: The {item} on them, the camera locked off. Sit them so the window lights one side of the face.

subject: Interview — tighter second angle
reason: The {item} gives you a second size from the same spot, so you can cut mid-answer.

fallback.subject: Interview — reframe tighter between questions
fallback.reason: One lens — reframe tighter between questions and you'll still have a cut point.

subject: Them at work, observed — you're not there
reason: Stay wide and quiet until they forget the camera. Five minutes before you roll is normal.

subject: Their hands at work, close
reason: The {item} gets you close without getting in their way.

fallback.subject: Their hands at work, from beside them
fallback.reason: No long lens — ask if you can stand close for thirty seconds.

subject: A still portrait — they look at the lens for five seconds
reason: Locked off on the {item}. Ask them not to smile. Five seconds feels long; it's the shot people remember.

subject: The outside of where it happens
reason: The audience needs to know where they are before they go inside.

subject: Timelapse — people moving through the space
reason: The {item} holds still for the length of it; the power bank keeps it running.
